structures.name: World Economic Outlook (WEO)
structures.description: The World Economic Outlook (WEO) database is created during the biannual WEO exercise, which begins in January and June of each year and results in the April and September/October WEO publication. Selected series from the publication are available in a database format.

values.name: Current account balance (credit less debit), US dollar
values.description: The current account balance is the balance of current transactions (transactions in goods and services, earned income and transfer income) between residents and non-residents. The term current account balance is used in the external accounts and is expressed from the perspective of resident units. The term current external balance is used in the national accounts and is expressed from the perspective of the non-resident units, and therefore with the opposite sign.

values.name: Annual
values.description: To be used for data collected or disseminated every year.

dataset.name: DOI
dataset.description: A public identifier (unique alphanumeric string) assigned to a digital object, typically a publication or dataset, to provide a persistent link to its location on the internet.Users use it for citing the resource.

dataset.name: Full Description
dataset.description: A comprehensive description of the dataset, encompassing its content, scope, underlying concepts, coverage, classifications, and statistical techniques employed in its creation and analysis. This may include references to detailed methodological documents or papers that provide further elaboration on these aspects.

values.id: The World Economic Outlook (WEO) database contains selected macroeconomic data series from the statistical appendix of the World Economic Outlook report, which presents the IMF staff's analysis and projections of economic developments at the global level, in major country groups and in many individual countries. The WEO is released in April and September/October each year. Use this database to find data on national accounts, gross domestic product (GDP), inflation, unemployment rates, balance of payments, fiscal indicators, trade for countries and country groups (aggregates), and commodity prices whose data are reported by the IMF. Data are available from 1980 to the present, and projections are given for the next two years. Additionally, medium-term projections are available for selected indicators. For some countries, data are incomplete or unavailable for certain years.

dataset.name: Author
dataset.description: The person or organization responsible for resource's substantive and intellectual content.

dataset.name: Publisher
dataset.description: The organization or institution responsible for making a resource available to the public or a specific audience. For datasets, the publisher is responsible for preparing and releasing the dataset for public or private use. This includes ensuring the dataset's quality, accuracy, and accessibility.

dataset.name: Department
dataset.description: The specific division or unit within an organization (e.g., the IMF) that is ultimately accountable for the creation, maintenance, and dissemination of a resource.

dataset.name: Contact Point
dataset.description: The primary individual or group responsible for handling inquiries and providing information about a resource. For datasets published on the IMF data portal, the point of contact shown to public users is standardized as a common help email address.

dataset.name: Topic Dataset
dataset.description: A topic of the dataset.  A high-level categorization of the dataset's subject matter, indicating the main area or domain to which the data pertains.

dataset.name: Keywords Dataset
dataset.description: A set of words or phrases that describe the content and subject matter of a dataset.

dataset.name: Language
dataset.description: It refers to the language of the intellectual content of the resource. It can be applied to any type of resource, including documents, datasets, images, audio recordings, etc.

dataset.name: Publication Date
dataset.description: The date when a resource was formally issued or made available to the public or a specific audience. This applies to datasets that have major releases, but the data may have minor updates throughout the year. In most cases where the data is regularly updated, the publication date is the same as the update date.

dataset.name: Update Date
dataset.description: The most recent date on which a resource was modified or updated, including changes to data or metadata.  For a dataset, the update date is the time when the data within a dataset was last modified, or the metadata was modified.

dataset.name: Access and Sharing Level
dataset.description: A classification that specifies the extent to which a resource can be shared with others, including restrictions on access, use, and distribution.  It specifies who can access the data (e.g., public, specific groups, authorized personnel) and what actions they can take with it. The appropriate sharing level depends on the sensitivity and intended use of the data, ranging from open access for public data to restricted access for confidential information. This attribute is assigned at lower levels of data when a dataset contains a mix of data access levels, with some series designated as public and others as restricted.

values.name: Public (Unrestricted)
values.description: Share this data with the public without restrictions.

dataset.name: Access and Sharing Notes
dataset.description: Additional notes involves documenting any нюances or complexities beyond the standard access and sharing levels.

dataset.name: Security Classification
dataset.description: A data classification assigned to data based on its sensitivity, value, and the potential impact of unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction, resulting in the assignment of a tag that designates the data's sensitivity level.  This attribute is assigned at lower levels of data when a dataset contains a mix of data access levels, with some series designated as public and others as confidential.

values.name: Public or Unrestricted
values.description: Information that has been published in full by the Fund and has been approved to be made available inside and outside the Fund without restriction is "Public" or "Unclassified."

dataset.name: Short Source Citation
dataset.description: A brief reference to the source of data or information used in a resource, typically including the author, title, and year of publication.

dataset.name: Full Source Citation
dataset.description: A complete reference to the source of data or information used in a resource, providing all necessary details to locate and verify the original source.

dataset.name: License
dataset.description: Information on the licence for distribution /  legal agreement that defines the terms under which a resource can be used, shared, or distributed.

series.name: Functional category
series.description: A classification used to categorize investments based on their purpose or function, such as equity investments, debt investments, or other investments.

series.name: International Accounts Item
series.description: A classification of transactions in the balance of payments, such as trade in goods, services, income, and financial flows.

series.name: Stocks, Transactions, Other Flows
series.description: A classification of data items used in the System of National Accounts (SNA) framework, distinguishing between stocks (levels at a point in time), transactions (changes over a period), and other flows.

series.name: GFS Stocks, Transactions, Other Flows
series.description: A classification of data items used in the Government Finance Statistics (GFS) framework, distinguishing between stocks (levels at a point in time), transactions (changes over a period), and other flows.

series.name: Expenditure Category
series.description: The Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 1999 is a standardized classification system developed by the United Nations Statistics Division to categorize household consumption expenditures by purpose. It includes 14 divisions, 47 groups, and 117 classes.

series.name: Trade flow
series.description: Data related to the movement of goods and services between countries, including exports and imports.

series.name: Commodity
series.description: Comprehensive list of all the different commodity codes used in IMF.

series.name: Social Concepts
series.description: A broad category encompassing various social indicators, such as tourism and labor concepts.

series.name: Sector
series.description: A classification of economic entities based on their primary function and economic behavior, such as households, corporations, government, or non-profit institutions.

series.name: Accounting Entry
series.description: A classification that identifies whether a transaction represents a use of resources, a source of funds, an asset, a liability, or a change in equity.

series.name: Index type
series.description: Type of index prices.

series.name: Prices
series.description: Represents different types of prices or price adjustments, including those that have been adjusted for inflation (real or constant prices) and those that have not (nominal or current prices). It also includes various methods for adjusting prices for inflation, such as using deflators or converting to a constant base period.

series.name: Statistical Measures
series.description: Describe characteristics of a group of data. They summarize the distribution, central tendency, or spread of multiple values.

series.name: Exchange Rate
series.description: Represents a set of codes identifying the exchange rate between two currencies. An exchange rate indicates how much of one currency is needed to buy one unit of another currency.  It is derived by comparing the value of one currency to another, often influenced by economic factors like interest rates, inflation, and government policy. This codelist includes various exchange rate calculations, such as period averages, pre-Euro rates, and those involving Special Drawing Rights (SDRs).

series.name: Transformation
series.description: Represents a set of codes identifying the specific transformations or calculations applied to source data to derive new data elements or indicators. A transformation involves a computation with one or more input values (either base variables obtained by observation or derived variables from prior transformations) that results in a single output value (the value of a new derived variable).

series.name: Unit of Measure
series.description: The standard unit used to quantify a particular data element or indicator.I It encompasses various units, including currency, physical units, percentages, and other standardized measures.

series.name: Reporting Period Type
series.description: It is used to identify and distinguish between different types of time periods in economic and financial reporting.  The specific start and end dates for a fiscal year (FY) can vary depending on the country, organization, or industry. When reporting data using this codelist, it is essential to specify the exact start and end dates of the fiscal year being referenced.

series.name: IMF Data Overlap
series.description: Indicates the potential for overlap within IMF data.

series.name: Topic
series.description: A topic of the resource. A high-level categorization of the resource's subject matter, indicating the main area or domain to which the data pertains.

series.name: Keywords
series.description: A set of words or phrases that describe the content and subject matter of a dataset.

series.name: Key Indicator
series.description: A flag or indicator that identifies a data element or indicator as being of particular importance or significance for a specific analysis or purpose.

series.name: Series Name
series.description: A  label  given to a specific series. This name helps to distinguish it from other series data and provides context for what the data represents.

series.name: Latest Actual Annual Data
series.description: This indicates that latest annual period for which official statistics are available from the authorities.  Data following this period are normal staff estimates.

series.name: Fiscal Sector: Instruments included in gross and net debt

observation.name: Derivation Type
observation.description: Identifies the specific method used to derive a new data element or indicator from source data.

observation.name: Source Organization
observation.description: The entity responsible for producing or collecting the original data used in a resource. This could be a government agency, a research institution, a private company, or any other entity that generates data. When citing or referencing information, it is important to identify the source organization to ensure credibility and accuracy.
